amended: 2026-11-06, after the first round-2 development fit (kept in output/soil_fertility_round2_20261106/superseded_fit_A) and BEFORE any Broadbalk 1926-1967 grain value was read. This is the only amendment of round 2; the evaluation is run on the refit whatever it shows.
reason: Development showed the bare-fallow benefit about four times too large (wheat after fallow 1.64 vs continuous 1.02 t/ha over 1867-1925, against +0.14 observed in the Alternate Wheat and Fallow experiment) and Broadbalk plot 3 overpredicted (1.03 vs 0.76). Cause: the plan's uptake rule lets a seedling take a fixed fraction of the mineral pool every vegetated month, so an autumn-sown crop after fallow captures the fallow's mineralized N before winter leaching. Real winter wheat takes up only a small share of its season's N before spring growth (stem extension, GS30-31), most between April and anthesis.
change: Uptake is also limited by a cumulative crop N-demand curve: by the end of each month the season's uptake may not exceed demand x fraction. Winter wheat (end of Oct..Jul): 0.02, 0.05, 0.07, 0.09, 0.12, 0.20, 0.40, 0.70, 0.95, 1.00. Spring barley and oats (Apr..Jul): 0.15, 0.55, 0.90, 1.00. Potatoes (May..Sep): 0.10, 0.40, 0.75, 0.95, 1.00. Shape from the UK wheat N-uptake pattern (HGCA Wheat Growth Guide, Sylvester-Bradley et al. 2008: little N before stem extension, most between GS31 and anthesis), declared, not fitted. Everything else in plan_round2.json is unchanged; the same five parameters are refitted with the same procedure.
source: Sylvester-Bradley, R., Berry, P., Blake, J., Kindred, D., Spink, J., Bingham, I., McVittie, J. and Foulkes, J. (2008). The Wheat Growth Guide. HGCA, London.
